title: Grateful Dead Live at Oregon State University on 1970-01-17
lineage: Master Soundboard Reel > DAT > CDR > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with occasional distortion and pitch slowdown, but captures a stellar early‑'70 show highlighted by a smoking Good Lovin', Mason’s Children, Dark Star and The Eleven.
ai_review.review: The tape, sourced from the soundboard, is generally listenable despite some muddiness, speed/pitch issues and brief drop‑outs. Musically the concert shines – fans rave about the tight groove on Good Lovin’, a powerful Mason’s Children, an inspired Dark Star and a memorable The Eleven, with strong vocals on High Time and a soaring Love Light.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and praise the performance; technical flaws are noted but do not dominate, yielding an overall high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Slight distortion in places, occasional drop‑outs, a half‑step slower pitch on the tape, but overall clear enough for enjoyable listening.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑'70 set with a tight first half and a soaring second set; jams flow naturally from St. Stephen into The Eleven, then into Love Light, showcasing the band’s developing improvisational chemistry.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Jerry's guitar work is noted as strong, especially cutting loose after Bob's solo on Hard To Handle.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass is mentioned indirectly via discussion of The Eleven being 'too hard' and possibly the last time they played it.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob added a brief solo before Jerry’s lead on Hard To Handle, highlighted as a noteworthy moment.
band_member_comments.Keys: The Hammond organ has an unusual tone—identified as coming from a Baptist church—which gives the show a distinct ’67 vibe.
